title: Gong ageng
summary: The gong ageng is the largest gong of a Javanese gamelan: a great bronze disc hung from cords in a carved frame. One deep stroke marks the end of a long musical cycle, and its slow, beating tone seems to hold the whole orchestra together.
howToPlay: Three places on the great gong are lit: Boss for the low centre, Face for the body, Rim for the bright edge.
Strike the place a closing ring marks. The gong swings and its tone slowly beats.
Hold your rhythm: the deepest strokes fall far apart, so wait for them.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A great hung gong marks the largest turn of a gamelan piece. Its tone is made to bloom slowly, so players strike it once and let it sing.
credits: Tradition: the gong ageng of Javan gamelan; patterns written for this game
